description: Fig. 10 is a four-panel composite of back-scattered SEM micrographs showing crack vertical sections of fracture-toughness specimens; the four panels are of the same type but at two magnifications. (a) and (b) are low-magnification views (scale bar 50 μm) carrying yellow "Main Crack" and "Matrix" labels; a cyan dashed line traces the main crack path and a blue dashed rectangle marks the region re-imaged in (c)/(d). In (a) the 0Al-steel crack runs almost straight with only gentle undulations, and a blue arrow labelled "Micro-void" points to a void just beneath the path. In (b) the 1.3Al-steel traced path shows frequent sharp deflections/steps, with a "Micro-void" arrow at the right. (c) is the 10 μm-scale magnified box of (a): a narrow crack branch penetrates into the matrix and ends in a small void, annotated "Tip passivation" by a blue arrow. (d) is the 10 μm-scale magnified box of (b): blue arrows label "Secondary crack" and "Micro-void", showing elongated voids and fine interconnecting cracks in the matrix below the main crack. Together the panels demonstrate that the Al-bearing steel delocalises damage by crack deflection, void formation/coalescence and crack-tip blunting, while 0Al propagates straighter. No numeric values are printed except scale bars.

void distance below main crack (μm) — stated in citing text, not printed on figure

observations.observation: The figure is a composite of four grayscale SEM micrographs, two at 50 μm scale bar ((a),(b)) and two at 10 μm scale bar ((c),(d)); (c) and (d) are magnified views of the blue-boxed regions in (a) and (b) respectively.
In (a) (0Al steel) the main crack path, marked by a cyan dashed line, is nearly straight with only gentle undulations and no marked branching.
In (b) (1.3Al steel) the cyan-traced main crack shows repeated sharp deflections and steps along its length.
A blue arrow in (a) and again in (b) labels a "Micro-void" immediately beneath the main crack path.
Panel (c) shows a downward crack branch that terminates in a small void, annotated "Tip passivation", i.e. crack-tip blunting in the 0Al specimen.
Panel (d) contains arrow annotations for "Secondary crack" and "Micro-void", with elongated dark voids and fine cracks distributed in the matrix below the main crack.
The word "Matrix" appears in yellow in all four panels, marking the uncracked region below the fracture surface.
The caption states that (a, c) are the 0Al steel specimen and (b, d) the 1.3Al steel specimen, and that (c) and (d) are the magnified images marked by the blue box in (a) and (b).

The citing text states that cyan arrows trace the main crack paths in Fig. 10(a) and (b) — visible in the image as a cyan dashed trace, although the image shows it as a dashed line rather than discrete arrows.
The citing text asserts that the 1.3Al steel showed frequent crack deflections while the 0Al steel exhibited straighter propagation with minimal deviations, suggesting faster crack growth.

The citing text reports secondary cracks and voids measuring 5–10 μm located 8–18 μm below the main crack in the 1.3Al steel (Fig. 10(d)), with fine cracks interconnecting the voids; these numbers are not printed in the figure and the image does not confirm them.
The citing text states that the 0Al steel displayed few voids and negligible secondary cracking, with main cracks occasionally deflecting but rapidly blunting upon penetrating the matrix.

The citing text links this figure to a toughening mechanism in which void coalescence initiates secondary cracks, deflecting the main crack and increasing energy dissipation, and notes that Ep of the 1.3Al steel exceeds that of the 0Al by 4.6 J (Fig. 7).

subfigures.description: Low-magnification SEM micrograph of the 0Al steel fracture-toughness specimen vertical section (scale bar 50 μm). Yellow labels "Main Crack" and "Matrix"; a cyan dashed line traces an almost straight main crack and a blue dashed rectangle encloses the region magnified in (c). A blue arrow labelled "Micro-void" points to a small void just below the crack path.

Low-magnification SEM micrograph of the 1.3Al steel specimen (scale bar 50 μm). Cyan dashed line traces a main crack that deflects/steps much more frequently than in (a); blue dashed rectangle marks the region magnified in (d); blue arrows label "Micro-void" on the right; "Matrix" in yellow.

Magnified SEM micrograph (scale bar 10 μm) of the blue-boxed region of (a), 0Al steel. A narrow, dark crack branch descends into the matrix and terminates in a small void; a blue arrow labels this as "Tip passivation". "Matrix" labelled in yellow.

Magnified SEM micrograph (scale bar 10 μm) of the blue-boxed region of (b), 1.3Al steel. Two blue arrows label "Secondary crack" (upper-left) and three blue arrows label "Micro-void" pointing to elongated dark voids and fine interconnecting cracks in the matrix beneath the main crack; "Matrix" labelled in yellow.
